mission.heading: What we do
body: Hypertext Studio is a small design lab building sustainable, human-centered software. We work in a fourth mode: design research where the apparatus is a real product.

Each product is a sustained attempt to answer one design question. The product must work as a product first — paid software, real users, supported, in production. The research happens through that constraint, not despite it.
The studies we publish alongside each major release are the studio's intellectual contribution. The products are the apparatus.

about.title: About
about.lede: Hypertext Studio is a small design lab building sustainable, human-centered software. We are an LLC and a Public Benefit Corporation. We do not have investors, a runway, or a growth curve we are optimizing.

sections.heading: The fourth mode
sections.body:
Design practices usually operate in one of three modes. Client work, where the idea is constrained by what a client will pay for. Research and prototyping, where the idea is unconstrained but never tested at scale. Product company, where the idea bends toward growth and retention.

We work in a fourth mode: design research where the apparatus is a real product.

Each product is a sustained attempt to answer one design question. It must work as a product first — pays for itself, supports its users, deals with the App Store, the support tickets, the accessibility audits, the people using the software in ways the designer did not predict. The research happens through that constraint, not despite it. Design ideas are not real until they have survived users who did not sign up for the manifesto.

sections.heading: What we work on
sections.body:
LogDate asks what personal memory software looks like when it isn't designed for surveillance, feed extraction, or social validation. Curfew asks what it looks like to give people real, hard-edged control over their own attention — including the ability to revoke their own consent to their devices, before the impulse to use them arises. Termsly asks what informed consent would actually require, in UX terms, between digital services and the people who use them.

The products are conceptually independent. They are not a thematic suite. They share infrastructure where it makes sense; they answer different questions.

sections.heading: How we publish
sections.body:
Each product produces studies — design research write-ups tied to major feature releases. Not portfolio shots. Real research papers. Each describes a design question, the bets we made, what users taught us, what worked, what didn't, and what the experiment ultimately said about the question.

The studies live on hypertext.studio. Copies appear on Bluesky and the fediverse — POSSE: publish on own site, syndicate elsewhere.

sections.heading: What we are not
sections.body: Not a venture-scale startup. Not an agency or consultancy. Not a research lab that doesn't ship. Not a generative-AI-interface lab. Not a portfolio site disguised as a studio. Not a media company, content brand, or thought-leadership operation. Not a community or a movement. We are an organization that makes things.

sections.heading: Where we are
sections.body: Las Vegas, Nevada. Distributed when we need to be.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: What we collect when you visit hypertext.studio.

sections.heading: What we collect
sections.body:
We use Cloudflare Web Analytics to count aggregate page views, see which pages are popular, and understand which countries our readers are in. Cloudflare Web Analytics does not use cookies, does not track individual visitors, and does not share data with third parties.

That is everything we collect from your visit.

sections.heading: What we don't collect
sections.body: We don't use Google Analytics, Meta pixels, or any third-party tracker. We don't set cookies. We don't fingerprint your device. We don't sell, share, or rent any data.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body:
There is nothing about you specifically in our data. Nothing to opt out of, delete, or export. Your visit shows up in our aggregate count; your visit isn't traceable back to you.

If you'd rather not appear in the count at all, your browser's "Do Not Track" or "Global Privacy Control" signals are honored. You can also block the analytics endpoint at the network level (`static.cloudflareinsights.com`).

sections.heading: Email
sections.body: If you write to us, we'll have your email address until we delete the conversation. We will never add it to a mailing list or share it with anyone.

sections.heading: Webmentions
sections.body: If you publish a post on your own site that links to a page on hypertext.studio and your site sends us a webmention, we may display the URL of your post, your name, and a summary of your post alongside the referenced page. You can ask us to remove your mention at any time — write to hello@hypertext.studio.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.body: If we change anything about how the site collects data, we'll update this page and note the change in the colophon's last-modified date.
